mainTopic: Proving רבי אליעזר's rule from a כהן's wart, and wrapping a כהן's injured finger in the מקדש: extra garments (יתור בגדים) and barriers (חציצה)
overview: The גמרא looks for a source that רבי אליעזר holds: even when preparations for a מצוה (מכשירי מצוה) override שבת, we still change the method as much as possible. It brings a ברייתא: a fellow כהן may bite off a כהן's wart (יבלת) in the מקדש, but not with a tool, and the כהן may not do it himself. The גמרא first suggests the ברייתא could follow the רבנן, with the 'fellow כהן' detail reflecting only where the wart is. But then it asks why the רבנן would not allow removing the wart by hand. It concludes that only רבי אליעזר explains the ban on the hand, as a safeguard against using a tool. A new משנה follows: a כהן with an injured finger may wrap it with a reed (גמי) in the מקדש, but not outside it. The גמרא discusses whether a small sash (צלצול קטן) is also allowed, either as a question of an extra garment (יתור בגדים) or of a barrier (חציצה). It brings רב חסדא's size rule of 3x3 fingerbreadths. A second version of the dispute between רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא and רבי יוחנן begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The source: a ברייתא about a כהן with a wart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn רבי אליעזר's idea and quotes a ברייתא: a fellow כהן may bite off a כהן's wart.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the source? As it was taught in a ברייתא: a כהן who grew a wart may have his fellow כהן cut it off for him with his teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the idea it just mentioned about רבי אליעזר. It quotes a ברייתא that will serve as the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבלת disqualifies a כהן from doing the עבודה, so removing it is a preparation for a מצוה. The ברייתא allows another כהן to bite it off on שבת. The exact wording of this permission will be analyzed in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (What is the source?)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
A wart, which disqualifies a כהן from serving
His fellow (another כהן)

phrases.english: What is it (the source)? As it was taught:
phrases.notes: Refers back to the idea that רבי אליעזר still requires changing the method

phrases.english: A priest who grew a wart
phrases.notes: The wart makes him unfit to serve until it is removed

phrases.english: his fellow cuts it off for him with his teeth.
phrases.notes: On שבת, in the מקדש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim made on the previous amud about רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר holds we change the method as much as possible, even when מכשירי מצוה override שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about biting off a כהן's wart

steps.title: Reading the limits in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws two limits from the wording: only with teeth, not a tool, and only by a fellow כהן, not by the כהן himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: With his teeth, yes; with a tool, no. His fellow, yes; he himself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and points out two restrictions hidden in its wording. These limits set up the question of whose opinion the ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using teeth instead of a tool, and having someone else do it, are both less normal ways of cutting. The ברייתא seems to require these changes even though it is a מצוה need. The big question is why such changes would be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
No
With a tool
He himself

phrases.english: With his teeth, yes; with a tool, no.
phrases.notes: First limit: the method

phrases.english: His fellow, yes; he himself, no.
phrases.notes: Second limit: who does it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws precise inferences from the ברייתא quoted in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא permits removing the wart only by biting, and only by another כהן

steps.title: It cannot be the רבנן, since they would see no difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the ברייתא follows. If it is the רבנן, who say biting off a wart is only a שבות and שבות does not apply in the מקדש, why would it matter who does it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If you say it is the רבנן, and the reason is that we are in the מקדש: since the רבנן say that in general this is only forbidden as a שבות, then here, what difference does it make to me whether it is he or his fellow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify the author of the ברייתא. It shows that the רבנן cannot easily be the author, because the 'he himself, no' limit makes no sense for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the רבנן, biting off a wart is only a rabbinic prohibition (שבות), and rabbinic prohibitions do not apply in the מקדש. So whether the כהן bites it himself or his friend does, it is the same permitted שבות. The rule against doing it himself is left without a reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
If you say
A rabbinic שבת prohibition
In general (outside this special case)
What difference does it make to me?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two limits. The difficulty here is only about the 'he himself, no' limit. The 'tool, no' limit is discussed later, in Steps 7-9.

phrases.english: Whose (opinion) is it?
phrases.notes: Opens the search for the author

phrases.english: If you say the Rabbis, and (it is permitted because) in the Temple
phrases.notes: The principle that אין שבות במקדש

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן בְּעָלְמָא מִשּׁוּם שְׁבוּת —
phrases.english: since the Rabbis say that in general it is only due to a rabbinic prohibition
phrases.notes: Biting off a wart or nail is only rabbinic for them

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, מָה לִי הוּא מָה לִי חֲבֵירוֹ?
phrases.english: here, what is the difference to me whether he or his fellow (does it)?
phrases.notes: Neither should be forbidden in the מקדש

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the limits from step 2 fit the רבנן's view
steps.kashyaTarget: Attributing the ברייתא to the רבנן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the רבנן it is only a שבות, which is permitted in the מקדש, so there is no reason to forbid the כהן from doing it himself

steps.title: So it must be רבי אליעזר, who changes the method when possible
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must follow רבי אליעזר. He holds that biting off a wart is a Torah-level violation, yet he still requires changing the method to the least severe form, even though מכשירי מצוה override שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not רבי אליעזר, who says that in general one is liable to a חטאת? And here, even though preparations for a מצוה override שבת, as much as it is possible to change, we change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers רבי אליעזר as the author, which would prove the idea it was looking for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, removing one's own wart is a full מלאכה requiring a חטאת. Since he also holds that מכשירי מצוה override שבת, it could have been allowed outright. Yet the ברייתא lowers it to a mere שבות (by teeth, by another person), which shows he holds that we change the method whenever we can.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...?
Liable to bring a sin-offering (a Torah violation)
Preparations needed for a מצוה
Override שבת
As much as it is possible to change, we change

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that even when a מצוה overrides שבת, רבי אליעזר does not allow it freely. One must still pick the least severe method available.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: Proposed author

phrases.english: who says that in general one is liable to a sin-offering,
phrases.notes: Removing a wart or nail is a Torah-level violation for him

phrases.english: and here, even though
preparations for a מצוה override Shabbat,
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר's well-known view

phrases.english: as much as it is possible to change, we change.
phrases.notes: Biting, and by another person, makes it only a שבות

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the רבנן, proposes רבי אליעזר as the author, which proves the original claim
steps.raayaObject: רבי אליעזר holds כמה דאפשר לשנויי משנינן even when מכשירי מצוה override שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two limits in the ברייתא only make sense according to רבי אליעזר

steps.title: No, it can be the רבנן; it depends on where the wart is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא can follow the רבנן. It is talking about a wart in a spot the כהן cannot easily handle himself. If the wart were on his belly, he could indeed remove it himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really it is the רבנן, and if the wart grew on his belly, so too (he may remove it himself).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from רבי אליעזר. It shows the ברייתא can fit the רבנן after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'he himself, no' limit is not a halachic distinction. It is only a practical matter of where the wart is. The ברייתא describes a wart the כהן cannot reach well by himself, but on an easy spot like his belly he may remove it himself. So the ברייתא is no proof that רבי אליעזר requires changing the method.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / in truth
His belly
So too / indeed that is so

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the גמרא suggests the ברייתא could follow the רבנן, with 'a fellow כהן' reflecting only where the wart is. Steps 7-9 challenge this reading, and the גמרא ends by concluding that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: No: actually, (it is) the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: Rejects the proof

phrases.english: and if it grew on his belly, so too (he may remove it himself).
phrases.notes: The ברייתא refers to a spot he cannot easily reach himself

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 4 by answering the difficulty from step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof that the ברייתא must follow רבי אליעזר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'he himself, no' was a legal limit. It is really a practical one, depending on where the wart is.

steps.title: Defining the case: a wart the כהן cannot reach himself
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the defense of the רבנן reading, the גמרא sets the case as a wart on the back or elbow, which the כהן cannot remove himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where a wart grew on his back or on his elbow, so he himself cannot remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation from the last step. It defines exactly where the wart is, so that the ברייתא can still fit the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 asked why it matters who removes the wart if the act is only a שבות. The answer is practical, not legal. The ברייתא says a fellow כהן does it only because the wart is in a spot the כהן cannot reach himself.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that narrows the case)
A wart (literally a 'bite')
His back
His elbows
Cannot, is not able

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the כהן is forbidden to remove his own wart. He simply cannot reach it. On the רבנן reading, 'a fellow כהן' describes the situation. It is not a legal limit.

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where a wart grew on him
on his back or on his elbows,
where he himself cannot remove it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the דחיה of step 5 by defining the exact case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase 'a fellow כהן, not he himself' seemed to set a legal limit, which only makes sense for רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only reflects a wart on the back or elbow, where the כהן physically cannot reach it.

steps.title: If the רבנן, why not by hand? And it would settle רבי אלעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: under the רבנן, removing the wart by hand should be allowed. The ban on a tool would then prove רבי אלעזר's view that using a tool is liable according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if this is the רבנן, let the other כהן remove it by hand! And then you could settle the question in favor of רבי אלעזר, who said: the dispute is only about removing by hand, but with a tool, everyone agrees he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the ברייתא follows the רבנן. If it did, the ברייתא should allow using the hand, not only the teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, biting off a wart is only a שבות, and שבות is allowed in the מקדש, so using the hand should be fine too. The only remaining restriction would be against a tool. That would make sense only if a tool is a Torah-level act even for the רבנן, which is רבי אלעזר's view. Something we were unsure of should not be settled so easily from here, so the רבנן reading looks weak.

keyTerms.meaning: But if it is the רבנן
Let him remove it for him
And you would resolve (an open question)
An אמורא, not to be confused with the תנא רבי אליעזר
Everyone agrees he is liable (to bring a חטאת)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is a later אמורא, while רבי אליעזר is the תנא in the dispute. The names look almost the same, but they are different people.

phrases.english: But if it is the Rabbis,
let him remove it for him by hand,
and you would resolve the question in favor of Rabbi Elazar:
for Rabbi Elazar said:
the dispute is about removing by hand,
but with a tool, everyone agrees he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן reading proposed in steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא can follow the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the רבנן, the hand should be allowed. The only way to explain the ban on a tool would be רבי אלעזר's view, so the רבנן reading forces an unwanted conclusion.

steps.title: Counter-question: רבי אליעזר should also allow the hand
steps.stepSummary: The other side pushes back: by the same logic, רבי אליעזר should also allow removing the wart by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, for רבי אליעזר too, let him remove it by hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the last question around. The same problem, that the hand is not mentioned, seems to exist on the רבי אליעזר reading too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'with teeth' and leaves out the hand under any reading. So the missing hand cannot prove that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר rather than the רבנן. This tries to cancel the force of step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
Also
Let him remove it

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
according to Rabbi Eliezer also
let him remove it for him by hand!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge to the question of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument of step 7 that the missing hand points away from the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The problem applies equally to רבי אליעזר, so it cannot tell us which opinion the ברייתא follows.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר forbids the hand as a safeguard; the רבנן have no reason to
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the counter-question. רבי אליעזר forbids the hand because it could lead to using a tool, which is Torah-level for him. The רבנן have no such reason, so the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of argument is this? If you say it is רבי אליעזר, that explains why he made a decree against using the hand, because of a tool. But if you say it is the רבנן, let him remove it by hand, and there is nothing more to say.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects step 8 and brings back the force of step 7. It ends by concluding that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, removing with a tool is Torah-level, so he bans the hand as a fence against using a tool. For the רבנן, the whole act is only a שבות that is allowed in the מקדש, so they have no reason to ban the hand. Only רבי אליעזר can explain the ברייתא's 'teeth only' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What kind of argument is this? (rejecting a comparison)
It makes sense if
He decreed (made a protective ban)
Because of, as a safeguard against
And nothing more (to say), a closing formula

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about biting off a כהן's wart follows רבי אליעזר. He allows only the least severe method, teeth, and forbids even the hand as a safeguard against a tool. This shows that רבי אליעזר limits the method even for מכשירי מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the source for רבי אליעזר's principle: even when מכשירי מצוה override שבת, one must use the least severe method possible.

phrases.english: What is this comparison?
It makes sense if you say it is Rabbi Eliezer —
that is why he decreed against the hand because of a tool.
But if you say it is the Rabbis —
let him remove it for him by hand,
and nothing more needs to be said.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the counter-question of step 8 and confirms step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the counter-question that the missing hand is equally hard for רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It overlooks that רבי אליעזר has a reason to ban the hand, as a safeguard against a Torah-level tool, while the רבנן have none.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, so it is a valid source for his view that the method must be limited.

steps.title: New משנה: a כהן with an injured finger
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a כהן with an injured finger may wrap it with a reed in the מקדש but not outside it. If the purpose is to draw out blood, it is forbidden in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן who was injured on his finger may wrap a reed around it. This is allowed in the מקדש, but not in the country. If it is to draw out blood, it is forbidden here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a new case about a כהן's injury on שבת and the difference between the מקדש and everywhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, wrapping the finger hides the wound so the כהן can do the עבודה, and the rabbinic ban on healing on שבת is a שבות that does not apply in the מקדש. Outside the מקדש, the wrapping counts as forbidden healing. Drawing out blood is a more serious act, so it is forbidden even in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks a new משנה)
Was injured on his finger
Wraps
A reed, a soft water plant
The country, meaning anywhere outside the מקדש
Forbidden in both places

steps.confusionAlert: 'מדינה' here does not mean a country or state. It simply means anywhere outside the מקדש.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A priest who was injured on his finger —
may wrap a reed around it.
This is in the Temple, but not in the country.
If it is to draw out blood —
it is forbidden here and there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wrapping an injured finger with a reed is allowed in the מקדש but not outside it. Wrapping in order to draw out blood is forbidden everywhere.

steps.title: Only a reed is allowed, not a small sash
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא limits the משנה: only a reed (גמי) may be wrapped on the finger. A small sash (צלצול קטן) would count as an extra priestly garment (יתור בגדים).
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יהודה, the son of רבי חייא, said: The משנה only allowed a reed. But a small sash counts as an extra garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה from Step 10. רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא says the permission covers only a reed, not a small cloth sash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן must serve wearing exactly the בגדי כהונה the תורה prescribes. Adding a garment, even a small one, is called יתור בגדים and is forbidden. A reed is not a garment at all, so it is fine. A cloth sash looks like clothing, so it would count as an addition.

keyTerms.meaning: A reed or rush; a plain plant fiber, not clothing
A small sash or strip of cloth
Adding extra garments beyond the prescribed בגדי כהונה, which is forbidden
'They taught only...'; a formula that narrows a teaching to one case

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with the sash is not שבת. The issue here is the special dress rules for a כהן serving in the מקדש.

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the גמרא's discussion of the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiya, said:
They taught this only about a reed,
but a small sash
counts as an extra garment.
phrases.notes: An extra garment is forbidden for a כהן during the service.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא גֶּמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the משנה's permission to wrap a finger with a reed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a reed is allowed; a small sash is forbidden as יתור בגדים.

steps.title: An extra garment is only a problem where priestly garments are worn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says יתור בגדים only applies to a place on the body where the בגדי כהונה are worn. On the finger, even a sash is not an extra garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: 'Extra garment' only applies in a place where garments are worn. In a place where garments are not worn, it is not an extra garment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב יהודה. He says a sash on the finger is not an 'extra garment' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, a covering only counts as added clothing if it sits where the priestly clothes are worn, such as the body or the head. The hand has no priestly garment on it, so wrapping it adds nothing to the בגדי כהונה. In practice, רבי יוחנן would allow even a small sash on the finger.

keyTerms.meaning: In the place on the body where the priestly garments are worn
In a place where no priestly garments are worn, such as the hand
'They only said... [when]'; a formula that limits the scope of a rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real disagreement about how far the ban on extra garments reaches. That disagreement decides whether a cloth bandage is ever allowed during the service.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
They did not say 'extra garment'
except in a place where the garments are worn,
but in a place where the garments are not worn,
it is not an extra garment.
phrases.notes: So a sash on the finger would be allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא אָמְרוּ יִתּוּר בְּגָדִים אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם בְּגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing view to רב יהודה about what counts as יתור בגדים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יתור בגדים applies only where the priestly garments are worn, so a sash on the hand is permitted.

steps.title: Shouldn't the bandage be forbidden as a barrier?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why discuss 'extra garments' at all? Any bandage, reed or sash, should be forbidden as a חציצה between the כהן's hand and the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him derive that it is forbidden because it is a barrier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole discussion. It suggests that any wrapping on the hand should be forbidden for a different reason: it is a barrier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the service, nothing may separate the כהן's hand from the holy vessel or the offering. That kind of separation is called חציצה, and it invalidates the עבודה. If so, even the reed the משנה allowed should be forbidden, and the question of 'extra garment' would not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let him derive it from...'; asks why a simpler reason was not used
A barrier between the כהן's body and the עבודה, which invalidates the service

phrases.english: But let him derive [that it is forbidden] because of a barrier!
phrases.notes: Both the reed and the sash would block the hand from the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה and both views by raising a separate reason to forbid any wrapping.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to wrap with a reed, and the debate about יתור בגדים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Any wrapping on the hand blocks contact with the עבודה and should be forbidden as חציצה, regardless of whether it counts as clothing.

steps.title: The wound is on the left hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the wound is on the left hand. The עבודה is done with the right hand, so a bandage on the left is not a barrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The wound is] on the left [hand].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the barrier question. The case is a cut on the left hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The service in the מקדש is done with the right hand. A bandage on the left hand does not stand between the כהן and the עבודה, so חציצה is not an issue. That is why the only question left is whether the wrapping counts as an extra garment.

keyTerms.meaning: The left hand, which is not used for the עבודה

phrases.english: [It is] on the left [hand].
phrases.notes: The service is done only with the right hand, so a left-hand bandage is not a barrier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חציצה challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bandage is on a hand used for the service, so it should be a barrier.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bandage is on the left hand, which is not used for the עבודה, so there is no barrier.

steps.title: Or on the right hand, but not where it touches the service
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a second answer. The wound may be on the right hand, but on a spot not used in the עבודה, so it is still not a barrier.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively, it is on the right hand, but not in the place used for the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer the barrier question. Even a right-hand bandage is fine if it sits on a part of the hand that does not touch the vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חציצה only matters where the hand actually makes contact with the עבודה. If the wound is on a part of the right hand that is not used to hold the vessel, nothing is blocked. So the משנה's permission can apply even to the right hand.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Alternatively'; introduces a second possible answer
The right hand, the hand used for the עבודה
The part of the hand that actually performs the service

steps.whatToRemember: A bandage on a כהן's finger raises two separate questions. Is it an extra garment? רב יהודה says a sash is; רבי יוחנן says nothing on the hand is. Is it a barrier? No, if it is on the left hand or on a spot of the right hand not used in the עבודה.

phrases.english: Alternatively, [it is] on the right [hand],
but not in the place used for the service.
phrases.notes: The bandage does not block the part of the hand that touches the vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי נָמֵי בְּיָמִין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹם עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, alternative answer to the חציצה challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bandage on the right hand must block the service.
steps.terutzMaskana: A right-hand bandage on a spot not used in the עבודה is not a barrier.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The bandage is not a חציצה, so the only issue is יתור בגדים, which רב יהודה and רבי יוחנן dispute.

steps.title: רבא quotes רב חסדא on when a covering is a problem
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רב חסדא: where the garments are worn, even one thread is a problem. Elsewhere, only a piece of 3x3 fingerbreadths is a problem, and anything smaller is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבא. רבא said in the name of רב חסדא: in a place where the priestly garments are worn, even one thread is a barrier. In a place where the garments are not worn, a piece of three by three fingerbreadths is a barrier, and less than three by three is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion that argues with what was just said about the bandage on the finger. רבא, quoting רב חסדא, gives a size rule for when an extra covering on a כהן becomes a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the idea was that on the finger, which is not covered by the priestly garments, a covering is not a problem. רב חסדא disagrees. Even outside the garment area there is a limit: a piece of 3x3 fingerbreadths is a problem. Only smaller pieces are allowed there, while inside the garment area even a single thread is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It argues, it disagrees
A place on the body where the priestly garments are worn
A single thread
It is a barrier, it causes a problem
Three by three fingerbreadths, the minimum size of a meaningful piece of cloth

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a two-level rule. Strict where the garments are worn, and a size limit elsewhere. The next steps test it against רבי יוחנן and רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rava,
for Rava said that Rav Chisda said:
In a place where the garments are worn —
even one thread interposes.
phrases.notes: Where the garments belong, nothing extra at all is allowed.

phrases.english: In a place where the garments are not worn,
three by three fingerbreadths — they interpose,

phrases.aramaic: פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ — אֵינָן חוֹצְצוֹת.
phrases.english: less than three by three — they do not interpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an opinion that disagrees with the lenient approach just reached about a covering outside the garment area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the garment area even one thread is a problem. Outside it, 3x3 fingerbreadths is a problem, and anything smaller is not.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא also argue with רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא clearly argues with רבי יוחנן. Does he also argue with רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא?
steps.simpleTranslation: With רבי יוחנן he certainly argues. With רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא, shall we say he argues?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares רב חסדא's rule to the two earlier opinions. It says he obviously argues with רבי יוחנן, then asks whether he also argues with רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said nothing is a problem outside the garment area, so a 3x3 limit there clearly contradicts him. רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא forbade a small sash on the finger, even though such a sash may be smaller than 3x3. By רב חסדא's measure that would seem to be allowed, so the question is whether these two opinions really clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly
Shall we say?
With, against (short for על ד־)

phrases.english: With Rabbi Yochanan it certainly disagrees.
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן allows anything outside the garment area.

phrases.english: With Rav Yehuda son of Rabbi Chiya,
shall we say it disagrees?
phrases.notes: He forbade a small sash, even one that might be smaller than 3x3.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וַדַּאי פְּלִיגָא. אַדְּרַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא מִי נֵימָא פְּלִיגָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב חסדא's new rule against the two earlier opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רב חסדא's 3x3 rule in conflict with רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא's ban on a small sash?

steps.title: A small sash is different because it is significant
steps.stepSummary: No conflict. A small sash is a significant item, so it counts even if it is smaller than 3x3.
steps.simpleTranslation: A small sash is different, because it is significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב חסדא and רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא do not have to argue. A small sash is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's 3x3 measure is for ordinary scraps of cloth. A small sash is a finished, meaningful item, so it counts as a real garment even below 3x3. That means both opinions can be true together.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
A small sash or band
Significant, considered important

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא definitely argues with רבי יוחנן. He does not have to argue with רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא, because a small sash is significant regardless of its size.

phrases.english: A small sash is different, since it is significant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 by treating the small sash as an exception to the size rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A small sash is significant, so it counts even below 3x3. There is no conflict with רב חסדא.

steps.title: Another version of רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא says the משנה's leniency is only for a reed, while a small sash is a barrier (חוצץ).
steps.simpleTranslation: Some report it in another version: רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא said, they taught this only about a reed, but a small sash is a barrier.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the ruling from step 11. In this version, the problem with a small sash is called a barrier (חציצה) instead of an extra garment (יתור בגדים).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical ruling stays the same: a reed is allowed and a small sash is not. What changes is the reason. In the first version, the sash was forbidden as an extra garment. In this version, it is forbidden because it blocks the כהן's hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version
Some say it, some report it
They taught this only about...
It is a barrier

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ruling. It is the same ruling from step 11, reported with a different reason: a barrier instead of an extra garment.

phrases.english: Another version — some say it like this:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda son of Rabbi Chiya said:
They taught this only about a reed,
but a small sash interposes.
phrases.notes: In this version the reason is חציצה (a barrier), not יתור בגדים (an extra garment).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 11 and records a different wording of רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a reed is allowed on the finger. A small sash is forbidden as a barrier (חציצה).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits small barriers to the area of the garments
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that an item smaller than 3x3 fingerbreadths counts as a חציצה only where the בגדי כהונה are worn. He then begins to explain what happens where the garments are not worn. That explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The rule that something smaller than three by three fingerbreadths is a barrier was said only about the place where the garments are worn. But in a place where the garments are not worn... (continued in the next section).
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the second version (from Step 19), the גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's response. In this version his rule is about חציצה, not יתור בגדים. The line sets up the next part, where he explains the law for spots the garments do not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is רבי יוחנן's statement in the second version (לישנא אחרינא) that began in Step 19. In this version, he agrees that even an item smaller than 3x3 is a barrier where the garments are worn. He is about to give a different rule for spots the garments do not cover.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrier or interposition. Something between the body and the garment that makes the wearing invalid.
Less than three by three fingerbreadths, the standard minimum size of a significant piece.
In the place of the garments, meaning the parts of the body the priestly garments cover.
'They only said this about...' A formula that limits an earlier rule to a narrow case.
Not in the place of the garments, meaning body areas the priestly garments do not cover.

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off in the middle. Do not assume רבי יוחנן says spots outside the garments are never a problem. The word אבל ('but') shows that a different, more detailed rule for those spots is coming next.
steps.whyThisMatters: Comparing this with Step 12 shows how the second version recasts the whole dispute between רב יהודה בריה דרבי חייא and רבי יוחנן as a question of חציצה rather than extra garments.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן's response in the second version, paralleling Step 12.

phrases.english: They did not say that there is interposition
phrases.notes: Opens a 'not... except' structure that limits the rule.

phrases.english: with an item less than three by three fingerbreadths
phrases.notes: This is about small items, below the normal size of a significant piece.

phrases.english: except in the place where the garments are worn,
phrases.notes: Where the garments are worn, even a small item is a barrier.

phrases.english: but in a place where the garments are not worn...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud with the rule for these spots.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא אָמְרוּ חֲצִיצָה בְּפָחוֹת מִשָּׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ אֶלָּא בִּמְקוֹם בְּגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the second version begun in Step 19, giving רבי יוחנן's response in that version. It parallels his first-version statement in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An item smaller than 3x3 fingerbreadths is a חציצה where the priestly garments are worn. For spots the garments do not cover, a separate rule applies, which continues in the next section.
